title: School Notebooks 5-pack

drivers.name: Price increase (2.3%)
drivers.evidence: Past weeks with same price: median x0.88 vs baseline; noise-adjusted estimate accounts for volatility and few observations

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 7.7. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price increased by 2.3% to $9.03, a level seen in prior weeks with low sales (e.g., 2026-09-28: 10 units, x1.03; 2026-10-05: 7 units, x0.78). The noise-adjusted effect of past price hikes at this level is x0.88. The heatwave (38°C) may reduce foot traffic, but no evidence links extreme heat to lower notebook demand. The classical uplift model gives 1.00, which aligns with no known drivers. The price increase is the only meaningful driver, with moderate evidence. Adjust downward slightly.

PRODUCT: School Notebooks 5-pack | category Office | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 (4 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 9.03 (+2.3% vs regular price 8.83)
  planner notes: Heatwave forecast: 38°C all week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 7.7 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 33.1 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 21.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-64% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
